01_mauriceville-bees-semi-texas.json.title: 2 Million Bees Escaped a Texas Semi. It Was Chaos.
01_mauriceville-bees-semi-texas.json.script: 2 million bees just escaped! Sunday morning in Mauriceville, Texas, a semi hauling 408 beehives took a turn too wide and tipped over — dumping an estimated 2 million bees onto Colony Drive. The driver walked away fine. The bees did not stay in the truck. Orange County Emergency Services ordered the entire neighborhood indoors while local beekeepers in full protective suits descended on the scene. The truck had been carrying 50,000 pounds of hive boxes. When it went over, the swarm was so thick responders could barely see through it. Beekeepers spent hours loading surviving hives onto replacement trucks, standing waist-deep in bees the whole time. Every recovered colony eventually made it to a local honey farm. The town of Mauriceville is going to need a moment. With 2 million bees on Colony Drive — would you have gone outside?

They'd left the doors and windows open, and apparently the snake saw an opportunity. When they finally found it, they called Stuart McKenzie of Sunshine Coast Snake Catchers 24/7. McKenzie arrived with a hook, reached behind the mount, and pulled the python out — calm, professional, utterly unbothered. The homeowner explained that the snake must have slipped in through an open door or window while they were airing out the place. Which is one way to describe almost sharing a couch with a python for who knows how long. The snake was released safely outdoors. How long had that snake been back there?

04_carol-oram-engagement-ring-michigan.j.script: 10 years inside a pipe! Carol Oram lost her engagement ring 10 years ago when a customer dropped it down a toilet at a shopping plaza in Hartland, Michigan — and it slipped into the drain before anyone could retrieve it. She gave up hope. Last week, plumbers from Titan Plumbing in Howell showed up for a routine sewer job at the same plaza. Inside the pipe, they spotted something shiny. They posted about it online. Carol's coworker Sue recognized the description and connected the dots. Carol and her husband — married 60 years — drove down to claim the ring. She cried. The plumbers had it professionally cleaned first, because 10 years in a sewer pipe does things to jewelry. What are the odds that ring survived 10 years in Hartland's plumbing?

05_tesla-autopilot-crash-katy-texas.json.script: Tesla drove into her house! On Friday evening in Katy, Texas, a Tesla Model 3 left the road and crashed through the side of a residential home. Inside was Martha Avila, 76 years old. She died from her injuries. The driver, Michael Butler, said he was using the car's Autopilot feature at the time — that the car was driving itself when it drifted out of its lane. A Ring doorbell camera recorded the moment of impact. Butler showed no signs of intoxication and is cooperating with investigators. The crash is now tied to a 3.2-million-vehicle federal probe by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, already at Engineering Analysis — the final step before a recall demand. A grandmother is dead. A 3.2-million-car recall is on the table. Was Autopilot to blame for Martha Avila's death?

06_seattle-dim-sum-guinness-record.json.title: Seattle Just Broke a World Record With 830 People Eating Dim Sum
06_seattle-dim-sum-guinness-record.json.script: The biggest dim sum ever! Seattle's Chinatown-International District gathered 830 people on a closed block of South King Street and broke the Guinness World Record for the world's largest dim sum gathering. The previous record was 764, set in Sydney in 2019. To qualify, everyone had to stay seated simultaneously — 900 showed up, but 70 stood up before the headcount and disqualified themselves. The dumplings came from Jade Garden restaurant, whose team hand-rolled 3,600 by hand. At 3:32 p.m., the Guinness adjudicator made it official. Seattle won. The neighborhood has dealt with years of safety concerns and gentrification pressure — and it answered with 830 people eating dumplings together in the street. How many of those 70 people who stood up early are regretting it right now?
